title: AEOeye vs LLMrefs: One-Off Audit or Weekly Keyword Tracking?
metaTitle: AEOeye vs LLMrefs: Which Should You Use? (2026)
metaDescription: AEOeye vs LLMrefs from public documentation: a free ChatGPT check and $29 one-time report versus a $79/month keyword tracker. Who should pick which.
shortAnswer: Pick LLMrefs if you need ongoing tracking: its single $79/month plan covers 500 prompts, eleven listed AI engines and weekly refreshes. Pick AEOeye if you first want to see where you stand today: a free three-question ChatGPT check, or a $29 one-time report that tests 10 questions on five engines. They are not substitutes. One monitors over time; the other is a snapshot showing the real answers.
intro:
This comparison is based on public documentation as of October 2026: LLMrefs' own pricing, FAQ and product pages. We have not used LLMrefs hands-on, and AEOeye is our product, so weigh what we say about it accordingly. Where LLMrefs doesn't publish a fact, we say so instead of guessing.

Most people asking "AEOeye or LLMrefs?" are really asking whether they need monitoring yet. Answer that first and the choice mostly makes itself. For LLMrefs on its own, see our [LLMrefs breakdown](/blog/llmrefs-review); for other options, see [LLMrefs alternatives](/alternatives/llmrefs).

sections.heading: Which should you choose, AEOeye or LLMrefs?
sections.body:
Choose by the job. If you must watch AI visibility every week, LLMrefs fits better. If you need to learn where you stand today, AEOeye is faster and cheaper.

- **Pick LLMrefs** if you work from SEO keyword lists, want weekly reports with share of voice and cited sources, and need many engines, countries or client projects under one subscription.
- **Pick AEOeye** if you have never measured this, want to read real answers from ChatGPT (free) or five engines ($29, once), and don't want a subscription.
- **Use both, in that order:** baseline with AEOeye, then add a tracker such as LLMrefs if the baseline shows something worth watching.

Our opinion: monitoring before a baseline is the common mistake. A dashboard tracking 500 prompts shows how a number moves; it can't tell you whether those were the right questions. Our [guide to AI visibility trackers](/blog/ai-visibility-tracker) covers how that category differs.

sections.heading: What is each tool built for?
sections.body:
LLMrefs is built for keyword-based tracking over time. AEOeye is built for a one-off audit of what AI engines say right now. The difference is the unit of measurement: keywords versus buyer questions.

LLMrefs says it tracks keywords, not prompts. You import or enter SEO keywords, it generates prompts from them, and it reports share of voice, position and cited sources per keyword ([LLMrefs homepage](https://llmrefs.com/)). That mirrors how engines work: [query fan-out](https://blog.google/products/search/ai-mode-search/) is Google's term for splitting one question into several related searches.

AEOeye starts from unbranded buyer questions. The free audit asks ChatGPT three of them live and shows the full answers, the competitors named instead and starter fixes. The $29 report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity and raises the count to 10 questions. Each engine runs at the default tier a free user gets. AEOeye is not a rank tracker.

sections.heading: How do they compare side by side?
sections.body: LLMrefs wins on engine count, ongoing history and data export. AEOeye wins on time to first answer, no subscription and a free first check. The table uses each product's own published facts as of 3 October 2026.

sections.heading: Where is LLMrefs stronger?
sections.body:
LLMrefs is stronger for continuous, broad tracking, and we would not talk a monitoring team out of it. Its published strengths are real:

- **Ongoing refresh.** Its FAQ says every keyword is updated in the dashboard "at least once per week", and weekly reports are part of the plan ([LLMrefs pricing](https://llmrefs.com/pricing)).
- **Engine breadth.** The homepage lists eleven engines, including Grok, Meta AI, DeepSeek, Copilot and Google AI Mode.
- **Scale.** Unlimited projects and team members, CSV export and API access, and monthly prompt-volume estimates sit in one plan.
- **Capacity per dollar.** 500 prompts for $79/month. Otterly's $29 Lite plan covers 15 prompts ([Otterly pricing](https://otterly.ai/pricing)); Peec AI's $95 Starter covers 50 ([Peec pricing](https://peec.ai/pricing)).

One thing to check yourself: the pricing card says geo-targeting in 50+ countries and 20+ languages, while a homepage section says 20+ countries and 10+ languages. Confirm which applies during the 7-day trial.

sections.heading: Where is AEOeye stronger, and what does it not do?
sections.body:
AEOeye is stronger when you want an answer now without a subscription. A free check shows full ChatGPT answers; the $29 report covers five engines once.

- **Free first answer.** Three buyer questions, asked live to ChatGPT, with answers shown in full.
- **One-off price.** $29 once versus $79 every month. Twelve months of LLMrefs is $948 (our arithmetic, assuming the price holds).
- **Default-tier testing.** We don't use stronger models than your buyers see.
- **Fixes included.** The report adds a 5-layer SEO foundation audit and a full fix roadmap, emailed as a PDF.

![Woman typing intently on a laptop at a home office desk surrounded by decor](https://images.pexels.com/photos/35730080/pexels-photo-35730080.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

The limits are just as real. AEOeye gives no history, no weekly refresh and no share-of-voice trend; to see change, you run it again. AI answers also vary between runs, and LLMrefs itself notes that models are non-deterministic, so one audit is a sample. In AEOeye's own audit records, only 157 of 892 engine answers (17.6%) named the audited brand; the samples are small and self-selected, so read [that benchmark](/resources/aeoeye-recommendation-benchmark-2026-09.json) as a reason to test your own questions, not as a ranking of engines.

sections.heading: What does each cost over a year?
sections.body:
AEOeye costs $0 to start and $29 once; LLMrefs costs $79 per month after a 7-day trial. The LLMrefs pricing page labels $79 "Limited time only", so budget for the price to change.

- **AEOeye:** $0 for the ChatGPT check; $29 one-time for the five-engine report. Run the full report again and you pay again.
- **LLMrefs:** $79 per month, $948 over twelve months at today's price. It lists no annual plan, and the price of extra keywords is not published (the FAQ says you can upgrade).

One $29 report is just over a third of one LLMrefs month. If you only need a baseline, that gap is the whole decision.

![Woman using a laptop indoors in a floral dress for remote work](https://images.pexels.com/photos/12498876/pexels-photo-12498876.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

sections.heading: How can you test the choice cheaply before paying?
sections.body:
Spend about an hour and no money: run the free audit, then trial the tracker with what you learned. This avoids paying $79 for a dashboard you won't act on.

1. Run the free audit on [the AEOeye homepage](/) and read the three ChatGPT answers. Note which competitors get named.
2. Turn each question into the keyword your buyers would search. See [an example report](/example) for what the answers look like.
3. Start LLMrefs' 7-day trial, add those keywords, and check whether its generated prompts resemble your buyers' wording.
4. Keep the tracker only if you will act on weekly changes. If you won't, a one-off $29 report each quarter or so may be enough.

sections.heading: What did we see on LLMrefs' own site?
sections.body:
We fetched LLMrefs' public files once on 3 October 2026 for AEOeye's [crawler access study](/resources/ai-crawler-access-study-2026-10.json). This is a neutral fact box, not a verdict on the product.

- **robots.txt** blocks only /account, /dashboard and /api, so AI crawlers can read the public pages ([robots.txt](https://llmrefs.com/robots.txt)).
- **llms.txt** exists at the site root.
- **Homepage JSON-LD** in the served HTML: Organization, WebSite and SoftwareApplication, plus contact and address details.
- **Documentation:** the Getting Started page said "Coming soon" when we checked ([docs](https://llmrefs.com/docs/getting-started)), and the free account's limits are not listed on the pricing page.

For comparison, aeoeye.com names six AI crawlers in robots.txt and carries FAQPage and Offer schema. One fetch on one day proves little; check both sites yourself.

keyTakeaways: Choose LLMrefs for continuous tracking: $79/month, 500 prompts, eleven listed engines, weekly refresh, CSV and API.
Choose AEOeye for a baseline: a free three-question ChatGPT check, or $29 once for 10 questions across five engines.
The free AEOeye audit covers ChatGPT only; Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity are in the $29 report.
LLMrefs labels its $79 price "Limited time only" and doesn't publish its free account's limits.
Baseline first, monitoring second: a tracker can't tell you whether you are tracking the right questions.

faqs.a: Neither wins outright; they do different jobs. LLMrefs is better for continuous keyword tracking across many engines at $79/month. AEOeye is better for a first look: a free ChatGPT check or a $29 one-time five-engine report. If you only need to know whether AI recommends you today, start with AEOeye; if you need weekly history, use LLMrefs.

faqs.q: Does LLMrefs have a free plan?
faqs.a: LLMrefs offers a free account with no credit card, and a 7-day free trial of its paid plan. Its pricing page doesn't list the free account's limits. Check the limit inside the dashboard before relying on the free account for anything real.

faqs.q: Is the AEOeye audit free for all five engines?
faqs.a: No. The free audit asks three buyer questions to ChatGPT only. The $29 one-time report adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity and raises the count to 10 questions. There is no subscription, and AEOeye is not a daily tracker.

faqs.q: How often does LLMrefs refresh data?
faqs.a: Its FAQ says every keyword is updated in the dashboard at least once per week, and that results are checked in real time. Weekly reports are part of the $79 plan. It doesn't publish a daily option on the pages we read, so confirm cadence in the trial if you need faster updates.

faqs.q: Can I use AEOeye and LLMrefs together?
faqs.a: Yes, and in that order. Run the AEOeye audit first to see which questions your brand misses and who gets named instead. Then, if you need ongoing monitoring, track those questions' keywords in LLMrefs or another tracker and re-check against a fresh AEOeye report later.
